about.body1: ShrinkIt is a free online tool for resizing, compressing and converting images. It was built around one simple idea: your photos should never have to leave your device just to become smaller.
about.body2: Every operation — decoding, resizing, format conversion and download — happens locally in your browser using modern web APIs. There is no account, no upload queue and no server storing your files, because there is no server involved at all.

faq.a1: An image's file size is simply how much storage it takes up, measured in kilobytes (KB) or megabytes (MB). It depends on three things: the pixel dimensions (width × height), the file format, and the compression level. A 4000×3000 photo saved as a high-quality JPG can easily weigh 5 MB, while the same photo at 1200×900 with moderate quality can be under 200 KB.
faq.a2: Resizing changes the pixel dimensions — for example from 4000×3000 down to 1200×900 — which usually shrinks the file dramatically. Compression keeps the dimensions but throws away visual detail to save space; the “quality” setting controls how much. For the smallest files, combine both: resize to the dimensions you actually need, then pick a quality around 70–85.
faq.a3: A pixel is the smallest dot that makes up a digital image. More pixels mean more detail but also bigger files. When you resize by percentage, you are scaling every pixel dimension by that amount — 50% of a 2000×1000 image gives you 1000×500, which is one quarter of the pixels.
faq.a4: Nothing is uploaded. ShrinkIt runs entirely inside your browser: your image is decoded, resized and re-encoded on your own device, and the result is downloaded straight from memory. Closing the tab wipes everything — there is nothing to delete because nothing was ever stored anywhere else.
faq.a5: JPG is best for photos and gives the smallest files thanks to adjustable quality. PNG keeps every pixel perfectly (including transparency) but is larger — ideal for graphics and screenshots. WebP is the modern all-rounder: smaller than both for photos, with transparency support. GIF is mainly useful for simple graphics; pick it when you specifically need the .gif format.

privacy.intro: This page explains in plain language what happens to your images when you use ShrinkIt.
privacy.s1d: When you add an image, it is read into your browser's memory. Decoding, resizing, format conversion and the download are all performed locally on your device using standard web APIs (Canvas, Web Workers). At no point is your image transmitted to ShrinkIt or to any third party, because there is no server component to send it to.
privacy.s1t: 1. Your images never leave your device
privacy.s2d: ShrinkIt strips metadata (EXIF) from processed images by default, which removes things like camera model, GPS coordinates and timestamps. You can optionally keep the original metadata with the “Keep photo metadata (EXIF)” switch; even then, the data stays inside the file you download — it is never sent anywhere.
privacy.s3d: This site uses no analytics, no advertising trackers and no cookies for tracking. Your theme preference (light/dark) is stored only in your own browser's local storage. If you install ShrinkIt as an app, its offline cache also lives only on your device.
privacy.s4d: Because everything runs locally, closing the tab ends the story: there is no account to delete and no server copy to request. If you have questions about this policy, reach out via the contact page.
privacy.s4t: 4. Nothing to delete, because nothing is stored
